episodes.204467: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms developed out ahead of a subtle upper level shortwave trough during the afternoon hours of August 18, 2025. Much of this activity did not reach severe limits, however a few thunderstorms in Christian, Webster, and Pulaski counties produced damaging winds, with reports of trees down and a damaged car port.
episodes.204472: An isolated thunderstorm developed during the mid afternoon hours and moved southwest through northern and western Jackson County, knocking down a tree at two locations between Skyline and Scottsboro.
episodes.204491: A traditional monsoon flow on the western flank of an upper level high over the central U.S. combined with daytime heating resulted in the development of shower and thunderstorm activity across the higher terrain during the early through late afternoon hours. Some of this shower and thunderstorm activity moved over the South Fork burn scar on both August 17th and August 18th resulting in flash flooding and debris flow across roadways on and downstream of the burn scar. Overall impacts were reported to be more severe and widespread on August 17th compared to August 18th. Finally, a brief landspout was observed in Las Vegas during the mid afternoon on August 18th as well as near the Bernalillo and Sandoval County line during the mid afternoon on August 19th.
episodes.204512: Developing severe thunderstorms quickly generated severe downburst wind gusts as they moved into Petroleum County.
episodes.204579: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204585: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204586: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204613: For a second consecutive afternoon, isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across the South Plains and Rolling Plains regions. The atmosphere was generally not favorable for severe weather but a relatively dry sub-cloud layer allowed one storm to become severe producing a severe wind gust. Although most storms did not produce severe weather, one storm did produce a severe wind gust near Levelland (Hockley County).
episodes.204741: Clusters of thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widely scattered instances of gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.205011: During the morning of August 18th, isolated thunderstorms developed in east-central Missouri. One of these thunderstorms became severe and caused damage to power lines and structures in Mexico.
episodes.205014: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of August 18th in a high instability and low shear environment. Conditions were primed for microbursts, and one such thunderstorm did produce damaging wind in southern Franklin County.
episodes.205382: Severe Thunderstorm Watch issued for Cheyenne County, with an isolated gust occurring in Box Butte County.
episodes.205504: A semi-line if thunderstorms tracked across the eastern Colorado plains, producing outflow winds up to 66 mph.
episodes.205930: A surface front was nudged southward across the local area through the day as high pressure strengthened north of the region. The front combined with high moisture, weak storm motion and diurnal instability with additional sea breeze forcing produced localized heavy rainfall across the area.
episodes.205931: A surface front was nudged southward across the local area through the day as high pressure strengthened north of the region. The front combined with high moisture, weak storm motion and diurnal instability with additional sea breeze forcing produced localized heavy rainfall across the area.
episodes.206062: A cluster of storms developed across eastern Colorado and led to wind gusts ranging from 60 mph to 72 mph across Kit Carson county with the strongest being 7 NNW Flagler. Dust storm conditions were also reported near Peconic and Idalia from the thunderstorm winds.
episodes.206082: Scattered storms developed west to east across the area leading to wind damage in Thomas and Logan counties including to a residence in Thomas county. Wind gusts of 60 and 64 mph were recorded at the Goodland Airport as well. A 68 mph wind gust was recorded 9 WSW Winona.
episodes.206142: Diurnal multi-cell thunderstorms produced observations of severe winds and wind damage across northern Oklahoma on the 18th.
episodes.206295: Although upper level ridging was in place, weak disturbances moving through the ridge resulted widely scattered showers and thunderstorms August 16 and 17. The stronger storms, which formed in deep inverted-V environments, resulted in a few instances of severe gusts, mainly across the eastern plains.
episodes.206334: During the evening of the 17th, a strong thunderstorm brought torrential rainfall to parts of LaSalle County.
episodes.206401: During the afternoon and evening of the 18th, a few rounds of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall to much of northern Illinois resulting in flash flooding. One particularly strong storm also produced damaging winds in DeKalb County. Initial reports estimate $8.8 million in flood damages around northern and northeast Illinois, and around $2.5 million in the city of Chicago alone.
episodes.206512: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across Northern Louisiana during the late afternoon and early evening on August 17th. As these thunderstorms and the associated outflow boundaries moved southwest, they encountered increasing instability with temperatures in the upper 90s to near 100 degrees and dewpoints in the lower 70s, yielding 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Despite the stronger instability, shear was quite weak. This weak shear resulted in very unorganized storms with numerous strong outflows. Strong storm cores supported the threat for microbursts, particularly where outflow boundary collisions occurred. As a result, a few thunderstorms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts across portions of Northeast Louisiana.
episodes.206579: Repeated rounds of rain led to increased saturation in soils during the month of August. As a result, when additional training storms moved over northeast Iowa during the morning hours on August 18th, numerous roads were flooded in Chickasaw and Winneshiek counties.
episodes.206582: Heavy rain during the middle of August resulted in minor river flooding along the Cedar River and on both Turtle and Dobbins Creeks.
episodes.206584: Heavy rain throughout the middle of August contributed to rises along many area rivers in northeast Iowa. This included minor to moderate flooding along portions of the Little Cedar and Cedar Rivers, as well as the Upper Iowa and Turkey Rivers.
episodes.206606: Thunderstorms developed over northwestern Nebraska along a surface trough of low pressure during the early evening hours of August 17th. This activity tracked east across northern Nebraska into the late evening hours producing hail up to golf ball size in the Ainsworth area. Quarter size hail was also reported in Sheridan County north of Ellsworth.
episodes.206637: A cold front was responsible for afternoon and evening thunderstorms. A few of these thunderstorms caused flash flooding.
episodes.206639: A cold front was responsible for afternoon and evening thunderstorms. A few of these thunderstorms caused flash flooding.
episodes.206660: A thunderstorm developed over Acadiana and produce a microburst that caused power outages.
episodes.206682: A pair of severe thunderstorms following in line passed through Divide County producing hail up to the size of golf balls. Significant crop damage was reported to the north-northwest of Appam.
episodes.206718: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across parts of Northern Louisiana during the afternoon on August 18th. These thunderstorms formed within an environment with slightly more favorable mid-level lapse rates of around 7 C/km and hot temperatures near 100 degrees. Weak deep layer shear of 10 knots or less limited storm organization, but despite the unorganized nature of the convection, very strong heating and instability supported strong to marginally severe thunderstorms capable of isolated microbursts and wind damage. As a result, a few instances of damaging wind gusts were reported across parts of Northern Louisiana.
episodes.206719: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across parts of Nacogdoches County during the afternoon on August 18th. These thunderstorms formed within an environment with slightly more favorable mid-level lapse rates of around 7 C/km and hot temperatures near 100 degrees. Weak deep layer shear of 10 knots or less limited storm organization, but despite the unorganized nature of the convection, very strong heating and instability supported strong to marginally severe thunderstorms capable of isolated microbursts and wind damage. As a result, a few instances of damaging wind gusts were reported across Nacogdoches County within the city limits of Nacogdoches.
episodes.206736: An upper high right over southern New Mexico trapped low level monsoonal moisture under it.  Overnight and afternoon thunderstorms were slow moving and heavy rain caused flash flooding near Rincon and La Union.
episodes.206744: Several individual rounds of thunderstorms impacted southern Minnesota from Friday, August 16th through Sunday, August 18th. Heavy rain amounts on the order of 5-10 inches fell over the course of 72 hours, most of which fell from late Saturday into early Sunday, leading to several cases of flooded roadways and damaged buildings. The highest amounts and most widespread impacts were across Waseca County.
episodes.206746: A cluster of storms developed near the Minnesota and Iowa border during the evening of August 17th, traveling northeast before dissipating near the Minnesota and Wisconsin border. A few storms exhibited strong rotation, producing a funnel cloud in Waseca County and thunderstorm wind damage in northern Blue Earth County.
episodes.206857: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce a lightning strike that injures one person near Seminole in Pinellas County, and produce street flooding stranding vehicles near Wildwood in Sumter County.
episodes.206927: An isolated thunderstorm over south central South Dakota developed within an axis of strong instability and DCAPE during the evening hours. Before weakening, an isolated severe wind gust occurred in northern Gregory County.
episodes.206934: Strong thunderstorms in Dewey County on the afternoon of August 18th produced severe winds.
episodes.206982: Thunderstorms developed over the James River Valley along a surface boundary.  These storms would pulse up and down quickly in strength as instability was elevated, but deep layer shear was very low. One storm did briefly become severe near Glenfield in Foster County, producing 59 mph wind gusts.
episodes.207042: Several individual rounds of thunderstorms impacted western Wisconsin from Friday, August 16th through Sunday, August 18th. Heavy rain amounts on the order of 5-7 inches fell over the course of 72 hours, most of which fell from late Saturday into early Sunday, leading to at least one flooded roadway in Pepin County.
episodes.207093: Moisture and instability pooled along a nearly stationary frontal boundary across southeast Virginia on August 18. Slow-moving showers and storms trained over the lower Virginia Peninsula region, with flash flooding occurring in the late afternoon and evenings hours.
episodes.207094: A weak trough aloft and weak surface low were located in the vicinity of southeast Virginia on August 19. Moist, easterly flow led to widespread showers with localized higher rainfall rates; the slow-moving showers on the Virginia Eastern Shore produced areas of flash flooding in the morning hours.
episodes.207186: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of August 18th through 20th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms.
episodes.207191: Major Hurricane Erin moved northeast and north of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Erin's Outer Bands and then Feeder Bands still affected the islands, producing strong thunderstorms, gusty winds, and heavy rains across the islands. Several reports of wind gust damage, along with reports of high surf, flooding and debris flow were received between August 16 to 18.
episodes.207233: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven and at times altered by sea breeze boundaries, and often producing locally strong and gusty winds. One storm near Mandeville reached severe limits, knocking down trees and powerlines.
episodes.207234: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven, producing locally strong and gusty winds. A couple storms produced severe marine wind gusts.
episodes.207235: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven, producing locally strong and gusty winds. One storm reached severe limits, knocking down trees and powerlines in Pointe Coupee Parish.
episodes.207315: High-based thunderstorms across southern Montana consistently produced gusts up to 66 mph.
episodes.207666: Beginning north of Webster Reservoir, a lonely severe thunderstorm drifted southeast across central Rooks County this lazy August evening. The storm dropped 1��� diameter hail just southwest of Webster and then produced 60 mph winds north of Plainville and at the Rooks County Airport. No damage was reported. The storm was really an anomaly in the area and formed in the high CAPE, lower shear environment. The storm weakened as sunset approached.
episodes.207667: Right in the middle of a line of thunderstorms along Highway 81 from Columbus to Hebron, heavy rain, hail and strong winds impacted the Shelby area shortly after 3:00 AM. A combination quarter to golf ball size hail and wind gusts near 60 mph were reported by the local NWS Cooperative Observer and local law enforcement. The thunderstorm quickly moved east into Butler county. ||This was a case which occurs fairly often in late summer in which a ���not-so-obvious��� shortwave, this time in southern South Dakota, triggers overnight thunderstorms. As the wave moved east, a low-level jet pushed moisture up the Highway 81 corridor while the weak upper winds became more favorably diluent in the area. Surface features were somewhat weak, but the night was unseasonably warm and 70 degree dewpoints had settled into eastern Nebraska. The brief intensification of the thunderstorm may have been aided by an outflow boundary pushing south across Highway 30 and into Polk county and into the back side of the thunderstorm line.
episodes.207668: A severe thunderstorm dropped ping pong ball sized hail southeast of Codell in southeast Rooks County around 5:30 PM. This particular storm was among a line of thunderstorms that formed along a weak surface warm front emanating east along Interstate 70 from low pressure in northeast Colorado. Surface based CAPE reached 4,000 J/kg as moisture pooled along the front. While upper forcing was limited, there was just enough energy from a weak shortwave moving east out of northeast Colorado to fire up the thunderstorms.
episodes.208229: A weak shortwave moved across Iowa overnight and through the morning of August 18th. And line of storms with trailing stratiform area passed across the state with the wave through the morning. MLCAPE was around 1500-2000 J/kg with a weak 850 mb low level jet sustaining storms. With weak effective shear around 20 kts or less, storms struggled to organize and did not become severe. As storms moved east, there was a pocket of enhanced low level stability with around 100 J/km of 0-3 km CAPE. This was enough to incur low level stretching and result in a few tornadoes in Grundy County. Tornadoes remained in open cropland and did not result in any structural or tree damage, identified by drone and satellite imagery.
